text:
ops-bot: PAGER ALERT -> inference-runtime: model-runner-prod (us-east-1) experiencing elevated 5xx rate (12% over 3m). Errors include OOMKilled and segfaults in model-runner process. Alert: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/ALERT-4799990000 :rotating_light:

ops-bot: Automatic incident channel created: #incidents (this thread) — priority P0.

dylan: ack @ops-bot I'm on it. Pulling logs and health metrics now. Will post preliminary impact in 5m.

infra-bot: k8s events show repeated pod evictions and OOMKilled on model-runner-rt-*. Recent events:
```
NAME                              READY  STATUS     RESTARTS   AGE
model-runner-rt-7f8b9d6c4-abcde   0/1    OOMKilled  3          2h
model-runner-rt-7f8b9d6c4-fghij   0/1    CrashLoop   5         1h
```
GPU driver notice: nvidia-driver reset on node gpu-us-east-1a-12.

sarah: seeing a pattern where crashes occur after long sequences with KV cache growth. Suspect quantized kernel path (fast_attention_q) hitting a bug under large sequence lengths.

mike: confirming: runtime native crash in cuda kernel. Extract from dmesg/core dump (sanitized):
```
[pid 12345] model-runner(+0x1f4a3) [0x7f8b9f4a3]
model_quant_kernel_init+0x2b1
kernel_fast_attention_q+0x9f
Segmentation fault (core dumped)
```
This matches a double-free we saw briefly in staging yesterday.

jia: any customer impact numbers? Support saw a spike in 500s for embeddings and generate endpoints. I have a list of affected customers (A-Enterprise, B-SaaS, C-ML) and a few open tickets.

katie: product: prioritize SLO customers. Can we route heavy customers to dedicated/different model variant (cpu fallback) while we mitigate? Need ETA for mitigation.

Dylan: proposed immediate mitigation plan:
1) Create temporary gateway routing rule to route traffic away from quant-kernel variant to fallback-model (cpu/float) for high-tier customers.
2) Set USE_QUANT_KERNEL=false env and rolling restart model-runner deployment to stop loading problematic kernel.
3) Increase gateway retries and slightly extend timeouts to reduce client-facing errors while restart occurs.
4) Capture core dumps and set up extended debug-level logs for 30m.
5) If instability persists, scale dedicated fallback pool and route 100% until kernel fix.

infra-bot: Executing gateway patch -> routes applied to ~18% of traffic (high-tier routing). Command: `deploy-bot apply-gateway-route --route-id tmp-fallback-4799 --percent=18`
Result: success.

ops-bot: Incident created and paged oncall: dylan (current). Severity: P0.

mike: stack trace shows free() called twice inside quant buffer free path (quant_buf_free). Will open hotfix branch to guard against double-free and to skip quant kernel on long sequences. Need a quick rollback/disable option.

sarah: starting core dump collection. Note: by default core dumps disabled on our GPUs — enabling now with sysctl and adding kernel.core_pattern to central bucket. This may require sudo on nodes. Coordinating with infra oncall.

Dylan: applying rolling restart with env flag now:
```
kubectl -n inference set env deployment/model-runner USE_QUANT_KERNEL=false
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-runner
```

infra-bot: rollout started: 60% pods restarted (10/16). No new OOMs reported for restarted pods yet.

katie: update: initial route + restart reduced errors for customers on fallback by a lot, but overall enterprise impact still visible. CS notified and reps assigned.

jia: posted an ETA note to affected customers: workaround routing in place, engineering investigating kernel. CS tickets opened and owners assigned.

mike: deployed hotfix candidate to staging to add an early-return when KV length > 16k tokens and to add safe-free guards. Running stress test (1000 long sequences). No segfaults in 30m so far.

Dylan: will canary hotfix to 10% of production (non-high-tier) for 15m, then escalate to 50% if stable. Patching production carries risk; fallback routing remains available to rollback traffic.

infra-bot: autoscaler note: cluster autoscaler added 3 nodes to handle eviction pressure. Nodes added: gpu-us-east-1a-21..23.

sarah: preliminary root cause hypothesis: a regression in the quantized attention kernel introduced in runtime v2.3 that manifests under large KV cache growth (long-context prompts) causing memory corruption -> OOM / segfault. Action: pin runtime to v2.2 on prod and block v2.3 rollouts until fix merged.

Dylan: mitigation status: routing + env-disable rolled out, rolling restart in progress, canary hotfix starting. Observed client 5xx rate decreased from 12% -> 1.3% in last 10m. Customer impact substantially reduced but not fully resolved.

ops-bot: Please prep for handoff. Oncall rotation: dylan's shift ends in ~45m. Next engineer oncall: mike-oncall will take lead for further mitigation and postmortem.

Dylan: Handoff notes for @mike-oncall:
- Watch prometheus queries: `sum(rate(model_runner_5xx[1m])) by (job)` and `model_kv_cache_size_bytes`
- Check /var/log/model-runtime/core* in s3 bucket for any new core dumps.
- If errors spike >3% revert routing to fallback fully and consider temporary capacity increase for dedicated pools.

mike-oncall: ack, taking over in 40m. Will keep monitoring and start postmortem doc after incident stabilizes.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations active, P0 -> monitoring. Next steps: continue canary, gather core dumps and logs, create postmortem skeleton.

(END OF THREAD)
